prospect.name: Jonathan
prospect.family_status: References his father, who told him he could do 20 pull-ups at the same age
prospect.training_background: Consistent for three and a half to four years, entirely self-directed. Started from Pavel Tsatsouline's 'Simple and Sinister', progressing one-handed swings from 35 lb to 80 lb and occasionally 90 lb, plus Turkish get-ups. Trains five times a week, 20-30 minutes, high intensity throughout — burpee blocks, EMOM work, man makers, running. Does one of Trevor's free YouTube sessions weekly: progressive EMOM two-handed swings at 90 lb for 30 minutes. Owns all his own kettlebells and describes himself as 'not a gym guy'. Can do 15 strict unassisted pull-ups. Has never followed anyone's programme through and has never had a coach. Self-describes as relatively fit and pretty thin.

signals: Self-directed and demonstrably capable — took himself from a 35 lb to a 90 lb one-handed swing off a book, with no coach ever
Anchored to a cheap alternative that genuinely worked: Pavel Tsatsouline's 'Simple and Sinister', a book, plus Trevor's own free YouTube content which he already uses weekly
Came to price-check rather than to buy — 'I'm poking around and seeing what the options are' and 'I was super curious what the pricing structure was for something like this'

Divergence worth noting: he displayed no skepticism about the method and never resisted the price, because the rep disqualified him before any close was attempted. the_optimizer is the alternative reading and fits his training profile, but his buying posture was comparison-shopping, not premium-seeking.

goals.text: Put on more muscle — explicitly not fat loss, he is already lean
Break a long-standing plateau at 15 pull-ups and reach 20
Get generally stronger and find out what it takes to push into levels of fitness he has never reached
Have a six-pack, which he has never had
Try structured coaching for the first time instead of assembling his own programmes

pains.text: Has failed at 15 pull-ups for years and does not know how to break through — 'I just fail every time for years... what does it take to build strength and break through these levels?'
Has never stuck with anyone's programme, always piecing together his own from books and videos
Cannot add muscle at his current bodyweight despite three and a half years of consistent work
Measuring himself against his father's claim of 20 pull-ups at the same age

tiers.label: Three-month tier offered live as the appropriate option for this prospect — 'We could do three months. That's 4K.' Not part of the documented offer.
Primal University Skool community — monthly, cancel anytime, three-month progression programme, weekly live session with Trevor. Second appearance of this tier in the batch.

evidence: The rep disqualified the prospect explicitly and early: 'obviously, you're not falling into our typical avatar of a client that Trevor works with... apart from you just like having an idea of leveling up and getting more stronger, there's nothing wrong with you.'

He then talked the prospect out of buying: 'I'm going to be honest, like, I don't want to sell you on something that's going to be so obvious and you're going to feel like, ah, so I spent 4K for this.'

He also told the prospect on the record that the programme's training format is not the right tool for the prospect's stated goal: 'when it's like 20-30 minutes and it's pretty explosive and intense, I don't think that's the way to build like a typical static strength of pull-ups.'
No close was attempted, no commitment sought, no follow-up scheduled.

Counter-evidence: the prospect asked for information on the $200/month Skool tier — 'Yeah, maybe send me the information on that' — so a downstream low-ticket conversion is possible. That is a different product and does not change this disposition.
The prospect never objected to anything. He came to price-check and left satisfied: 'Thanks for being real with me.'
outcome.next_step: Rep to email information on the $200/month Primal University community. Nothing else agreed.

notable.note: The cleanest disqualification in the batch and, judged as conduct rather than as revenue, the best call in it. The rep told a well-trained prospect he was outside the avatar, told him the programme's format would not solve his stated goal, refused to sell him something he would resent paying for, and then gave him the actual answer for free — band-assisted reps to break the psychological ceiling, then weighted pull-ups at five reps for strength. That is exactly the norm the sales manager stated on the 07/07 team meeting: 'You can't make something look big enough that isn't there.' Two costs, though. He disqualified without ever asking what the prospect does for a living, so the two commercial ICP criteria were never tested. And the honesty was delivered alongside two prices that do not exist in the documented offer — a three-month tier at $4,000 and the $200/month community.

quality.notes: Consistent inversion, including on the price statement itself. At 00:06:51-00:07:21 the rep's transparency preamble carries his own label but the price answer 'Well, usually it's $6,000' sits under it while the bracketing question is fragmented — the text reads 'Now, my question is…,000 or $10,000?' with a word dropped, so the exact figure he floated cannot be recovered. Other inversions at 00:01:16 (the rep's label carries the prospect's 'I'm just looking to put on a little bit more muscle'), 00:02:50, 00:03:45 ('I can't break through 15 pull-ups' is the prospect's), 00:04:54 and 00:14:30. Roles read from content throughout. No surname is ever spoken, so the call_id uses the given name only. The call is short but complete — it opens at 00:00:01 and closes naturally.
